title: Working at Redwood: roles, career ladders, benefits, hiring & onboarding, and internal tools
author: Avery Chen
body:
Overview

This page is the canonical Redwood handbook section covering: what it’s like to work at Redwood, our role definitions and career ladders, benefits & perks, end-to-end hiring and onboarding process, and the primary internal tools new hires and managers should know about. The intent is to provide clear expectations and a single place for People Ops to point new hires, managers, and interviewers.

Who this is for
- New hires (all levels)
- Hiring managers and interviewers
- People Ops partners and onboarding buddies
- Engineering and cross-functional leaders who need role definitions and promotion criteria

Quick links
- New hire checklist: /confluence/company-handbook/new-hire-checklist (internal)
- Interview guide and rubrics: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/support-top-issues/interview-rubrics
- Benefits FAQ: /confluence/company-handbook/benefits-faq-2026

Roles & career ladders (high level)
This section defines the role families used at Redwood and the expectations at each level. Each engineering and product team has a more detailed leveling rubric (see Related Resources).

Role families we use (examples)
- Engineering: IC (SWE), Staff/Principal, Engineering Manager, Senior Engineering Manager, Director
- Product: PM (IC), Senior PM, Group PM, Director PM
- Research/Applied ML: Researcher I/II, Senior Researcher, Staff Researcher
- GTM: SDR, AE, Senior AE, Sales Manager, Director Sales

Leveling summary (common expectations)
- IC-1 / L3 (Entry): Delivers tasks with close mentorship, demonstrates core product/domain knowledge, writes reliable code and tests.
- IC-2 / L4 (Mid): Owns features end-to-end, influences design within team, mentor to juniors.
- IC-3 / L5 (Senior): Designs systems, defines technical direction for multi-sprint work, strong cross-team collaboration.
- Staff / L6: Shapes architecture and standards across multiple teams, leads cross-functional initiatives, coaches senior engineers.
- Principal / L7+: Sets org-level technical strategy, represents Redwood externally on technical topics.

Promotion signals and evidence (used by managers and promotion committees)
1) Impact: measurable product or operational improvements (metrics, cost savings, latency improvements, customer outcomes).
2) Scope: owning cross-team/organizational areas, repeated delivery of high-impact initiatives.
3) Craft: technical depth, code quality, design docs, and consistent peer recognition.
4) Leadership: mentoring, recruiting, and enabling others; demonstrated decision-making in ambiguity.

Promotion process (summary)
1. Manager collects concrete examples and feedback (OKR/PR/incident notes).
2. Calibration meeting with manager’s peer group.
3. Promotion packet created: title, level, summary of evidence, reviewer list.
4. Promotion committee review and response within 3 weeks.

Benefits & perks (summary table)
| Category | Details | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Medical, Dental, Vision | Several plans (PPO/HMO) with company contribution up to 85% for medical premiums | Benefits vendor: BrightHealthPartners (portal login required) |
| 401(k) | 4% automatic match plus discretionary company contribution | Fidelity 401(k) portal |
| Paid time off | 20 days PTO (vesting after 6 months), 12 company holidays, parental leave: 16 weeks primary, 8 weeks secondary | Time-off requests via HRIS (Workday) |
| Learning & development | $3,000 annual L&D budget, monthly Lunch & Learn series | Submit reimbursements via L&D portal |
| Commuter / Remote stipend | Quarterly remote stipend $150 or commuter pre-tax benefit | Eligibility: full-time employees |
| Wellness & perks | Quarterly wellness stipend, mental health EAP, catered team budgets, conference allowance | See Benefits FAQ for details |

Taxable perks and policies
- Stipends are taxable and paid on regular payroll.
- Equipment: standard laptop + monitor; personal equipment reimbursements require prior approval.

Hiring & onboarding overview (end-to-end)
Objective: get a new hire fully productive and integrated in first 90 days while keeping time-to-productivity consistent across teams. Our SLAs: 
- Offer to acceptance turnaround: target 72 hours for compensation and approvals.
- New hire IT & account provisioning: complete within 3 business days after signed offer (SLO).
- First 1:1 with manager scheduled by day 3.

High-level hiring flow
1. Requisition & hiring plan created by manager and People Ops (includes role, level, interview panel, and diversity targets).
2. Sourcing & screening: recruiter screens, then passes to manager for technical screen scheduling.
3. Interview loop: standardized rubric used; interviewers submit feedback within 48 hours.
4. Debrief & calibration: panel meets to make a hire/no-hire decision and consensus on level.
5. Offer creation & approvals: People Ops creates offer with compensation band and approvals route.
6. Onboarding kickoff: People Ops sends welcome packet and schedules orientation.

Onboarding timeline (first 30 / 90 days)
- Pre-start (before day 0): welcome email, paperwork, equipment survey, Slack invite to #new-hires, buddy assigned.
- Day 0-3: IT provisioning, first 1:1 scheduled, HR orientation.
- Week 1: Team orientation, product overview, security training, access to core repos and dashboards.
- End of Week 2: First small deliverable or shadowing assignment.
- Month 1: Checkpoint 30-day review (manager + People Ops).
- Month 3: Formal 90-day review: performance, growth goals, onboarding feedback.

Manager checklist (first 2 weeks)
1. Schedule 1:1 cadence (recommended weekly for first 3 months).
2. Add new hire to active projects and assign initial small deliverable.
3. Ensure access to codebase, CI, monitoring, and staging.
4. Introduce buddy and schedule product walkthrough.
5. Provide first 30/90-day goals and success criteria.

Internal tools & guides (primary list)
- Slack (team communication): channels to join — #all-hands, #product-updates, #eng-announce, #new-hires.
- HRIS / Payroll: Workday (onboarding paperwork, time off, personal info).
- Single Sign-On: Okta (application access).
- Source control: GitHub (org: redwood-inference). Repos are grouped by service and team.
- CI/CD: CircleCI and internal deploy pipelines, documented in eng-infra/runbooks.
- Observability & incidents: Datadog (dashboards), Sentry (errors), PagerDuty (on-call rotations).
- Docs & knowledge base: Confluence (this space) — please keep team docs current and link to parent pages.
- Expense & budget: Concur for travel expenses, L&D reimbursements via internal L&D portal.

How to request access (standard flow)
1. Submit access request in Okta or the Access Request form: /confluence/policies-and-process/access-request-form.
2. Manager approves within 24 hours.
3. Platform/IT completes provisioning, notify owner when done.

First 90 days checklist (new hire friendly)
- Complete security & compliance training (required by day 7).
- Join team standups and complete at least one small code review.
- Deliver a scoped task that touches the codebase and CI pipeline.
- Schedule informational 1:1s with cross-functional partners (Product, SRE, Ops).
- Submit feedback on onboarding to People Ops via the onboarding survey.

Escalation & owners
- People Ops (onboarding coordinator): Priya Patel — priya.patel@redwood.example (primary contact for HR/offer questions).
- IT & provisioning: Marcus Rivera — it-ops@redwood.example (escalate provisioning > 3 business days).
- Security/compliance questions: Elena Gomez (security lead) — security@redwood.example.

Frequently asked questions
Q: Who sets the level for a hire?
A: The hiring manager proposes a level based on the role rubric; the interview panel and People Ops must agree before an offer is sent.

Q: What if a new hire needs additional setup time for hardware?
A: Managers should notify IT when an offer is accepted. For on-prem hardware requests, add two business days to the provisioning SLA and inform People Ops.

Q: How do I request a promotion?
A: Speak with your manager to gather evidence. The manager will prepare the promotion packet and route it to the promotion committee. Expect ~3-6 weeks for the full review.
